title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed by an attacker to conduct post-exploitation operations against Thailand's Ministry of Finance, running without human oversight in what researchers call "YOLO mode." The agent was used to enumerate hosts, escalate privileges, and gather data from the ministry's networks after initial compromise. The operator built specialized tools targeting the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure, GlassFish servers, and email systems, and deployed a custom implant called Hades.

The attack would have been detected earlier with network monitoring for the patterns of autonomous agent activity, restrictions on the use of default credentials and known exploits, and segmentation that limits lateral movement across internal systems. Researchers discovered the operation only through exposed directories on a separate Hong Kong server that contained the agent's logs, exploit code, webshells, and stolen credentials. It is not established how long the agent operated before detection or what data was ultimately exfiltrated.

summary:
# Summary

Attackers used an autonomous AI agent called Hermes to target Thailand's Ministry of Finance starting in mid-to-late June 2026. Researchers discovered exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing exploit code, webshells, stolen credentials, and logs showing the AI agent operating without human oversight in "YOLO mode." The operator, who appears to be a Chinese-speaking individual, deployed a custom implant called Hades and built specialized tools to attack the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure, GlassFish servers, and email systems.

The investigation revealed the attacker had detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal network topology and successfully compromised multiple systems using privilege escalation exploits and default credentials. Recovered files included active session cookies, malicious scripts targeting financial systems, and logs documenting the AI agent's activities as it enumerated hosts and gathered data about personnel records. Thailand's national CERT and security agency were notified on July 15, 2026. The attack demonstrates how criminals are increasingly delegating routine offensive operations to AI agents that can work autonomously without direct human monitoring.
